text: dsh-deepseek-search-account 是为 DSH 提供 DeepSeek 账号网页能力的插件。它在 web 接口注册搜索和抓取提供方，并由 bundle 将内置 web_search 与 web_fetch 指向这两个提供方。搜索默认调用官方 Search API，抓取调用 Fetch API，将页面内容作为 Markdown 返回；抓取无法取得正文时可使用本机 http 提供方回退。适合聊天模型通过第三方网关、但希望使用 DSH DeepSeek 账号完成网页检索的用户。需要登录 DeepSeek 账号，或配置 API key。

dsh-deepseek-search-account adds account backed web search and page fetching to DSH. It routes web_search and web_fetch through DeepSeek Search and Fetch APIs, with an optional local http fallback for pages the API cannot retrieve. Sign in to a DeepSeek account or configure an API key.
让 DSH 在聊天模型走第三方网关时也能搜索网页。
我想用已登录的 DeepSeek 账号抓取网页并读取 Markdown 内容。
Keep DSH web search and page fetching available when my chat model uses another provider.
dsh-deepseek-search-account 的功能「账号网页搜索」：把 DSH 的 web_search 路由到 DeepSeek Search API，使用账号认证并返回搜索结果。
dsh-deepseek-search-account 的功能「网页抓取」：把 web_fetch 路由到 DeepSeek Fetch API，返回页面 Markdown；官方抓取无法获取内容时可调用本机 http 提供方回退。
dsh-deepseek-search-account 使用前须知：搜索问题和目标网页 URL 会发送到 api.deepseek.com；抓取失败时默认还会由本机 http 提供方请求目标页面。

dsh-deepseek-search-account README · dsh-deepseek-search-account：[English](README.md) | [中文](README.zh.md)

A tiny DeepSeek Harness (DSH) plugin that keeps the built-in `web_search` and `web_fetch` tools working when your chat model is served by an **external, non-official subscription** — for example **OpenCode Go** (`opencode.ai/zen/go`), another Anthropic-compatible gateway, or a pi-ai provider — while DeepSeek Harness is signed in to a DeepSeek account.

dsh-deepseek-search-account README · dsh-deepseek-search-account：Search and page fetching then run on the official DeepSeek **Search / Fetch API using that DeepSeek account**, so both tools keep working without a `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY`.

dsh-deepseek-search-account README · When to use it / 适用情况：- Your DSH chat model is served by a third-party subscription or gateway (OpenCode Go / Zen, another Anthropic-compatible endpoint, pi-ai, etc.), not by a DeepSeek Account model.
- You are signed in to a DeepSeek account in DSH (Settings → Account), and that account may be used for search and fetching.
- The built-in web search fails with `DeepSeek search has no API key for "DEEPSEEK_API_KEY"`, and you do not have (or do not want to use) a DeepSeek API key.

text:
dsh-deepseek-search-account README · Why it is needed：The shipped search providers (`dsh-web-search-deepseek`, `dsh-web-deepseek-api`) only use the DeepSeek account sign-in when the **initiating session's model route** is `deepseek-account`:

```js
ctx.get("agents")?.currentInitiator()?.session.requestContext()?.provider === "deepseek-account"
```

dsh-deepseek-search-account README · Why it is needed：With OpenCode Go as the chat provider, that check fails, the provider falls back to the `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY` credential, and — with no key stored — `web_search` fails. This plugin resolves the same account token (`ctx.deepseekAccount.resolveToken(endpoint)`) on **every search and fetch**, without looking at the conversation's model route, and falls back to `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY` (Bearer) only when account sign-in is unavailable.

dsh-deepseek-search-account README · What it does：- Registers a search provider named `deepseek-account-search` and a fetch provider named `deepseek-account-fetch` on the `ctx.web` seam.
- Calls the official DeepSeek Search API (`POST https://api.deepseek.com/v1/tools/search`) by default — one HTTP request per search, about 0.5–1 second, returning `title`, `url`, `snippet` and `date`; no auxiliary model turn, no extra model tokens.
- Calls the official DeepSeek Fetch API (`POST https://api.deepseek.com/v1/tools/fetch`) for `web_fetch` — one HTTP request, the page body returned as Markdown, instead of the shipped anonymous `http` provider.
- Falls back to the locally mounted `http` provider when the DeepSeek crawler cannot retrieve a page (HTTP 403/404, raw text files, no extractable body), so `web_fetch` still works on those URLs; set `fallbackFetchProvider: none` to keep official fetching only.
- Keeps a legacy `mode: messages` search backend (Anthropic-compatible Messages endpoint + the native `web_search_20250305` server tool) as an explicit fallback.
- Ships a bundle patch (`cordis.patch.yml`) that registers both providers and pins `web.searchProvider` / `web.fetchProvider` to

After editing `provider.js`, restart DSH — or toggle the row `disabled: true` / back — to load the new code.

dsh-deepseek-search-account README · Configuration：Installed as a bundle, the row lives in this package's `cordis.patch.yml`. Override it from the profile patch with an id-targeted entry that repeats the row name:

```yaml
- id: web-search-deepseek-account
  name: dsh-deepseek-search-account
  config:
    mode: search-api

dsh-deepseek-search-account README · Configuration：| Key | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `mode` | `search-api` | Search backend: `search-api` = official Search API; `messages` = Anthropic Messages + `web_search_20250305` server tool |
| `baseURL` | `https://api.deepseek.com/v1/tools` | Search/Fetch API base URL (`/search` and `/fetch` are appended) |
| `count` | `10` | Results per Search API request, 1–50; the tool's `searchMaxResults` wins when smaller |
| `sendOriginalQuestion` | `true` | Send `ori_question` (the session's latest user prompt, ≤128 chars) |
| `fetchMaxChars` | `100000` | Cap on the Markdown characters one fetch returns (the seam marks the result truncated) |
| `fetchTimeoutMs` | `30000` | Provider-side timeout for one Fetch API request |
| `fallbackFetchProvider` | `http` | Local provider tried when the official Fetch API cannot retrieve a page; `none` disables the fallback |
| `apiKey` / `apiKeyEnv` | unset / `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY` | API-key fallback when account sign-in is unavailable |
| `messagesBaseURL` | `https://api.deepseek.com/anthropic/v1` | Only `mode: messages` (`/messages` is appended) |
| `model` | `deepseek-flash` | Only `mode: messages` |
|

dsh-deepseek-search-account README · Billing and quotas：- Both the Search and Fetch APIs bill **per successful request**: 5 CNY / 1000 successful requests (about 0.005 CNY per call), charged to the DeepSeek account since 2026-11-01 00:00 Beijing time. For search, only requests that return a non-empty `results` array are billed; for fetch, only requests that return page content. Failed requests and timeouts are not billed. See the official [Search & Fetch guide](https://api-docs.deepseek.com/zh-cn/guides/search/).
- Search and fetch **do not consume chat-model tokens** and do not touch the subscription used for chatting (e.g. OpenCode Go). Only the DeepSeek account's web quota is involved.
- Latency is about 0.5–1 s per search and about 0.2–1 s per fetch.
- Account-level rate limits are separate per API: Search 100 QPS, Fetch 25 QPS.
- `mode: messages` is different: one search costs a full auxiliary model turn (thousands of input tokens, 4–6 s), and server-tool searches are also billed per call as of the same date. Use it only as a fallback.

dsh-deepseek-search-account README · Security：- The DeepSeek account token is read from the DSH credential service per request (`ctx.deepseekAccount.resolveToken`) and sent only to the `api.deepseek.com` origin; the account service validates the origin.
- The plugin never writes the token to disk and never exposes it to the browser.
- Fetches are performed by DeepSeek's server, so the target URL leaves your machine to the DeepSeek API rather than being fetched locally. Only when the official fetch fails with a content error (403/404 or no body) does the page get fetched locally through the shipped `http` provider; pin `fetchProvider: http` or set `fallbackFetchProvider: none` if you never want local fetching.
- No runtime dependencies, no install scripts: plain ESM using `node:` built-ins and the global `fetch`.

dsh-deepseek-search-account README · Requirements：- DeepSeek Harness `0.2.1-rc.5` or later (the `ctx.web` seam and `deepseekAccount` service it relies on).
- Signed in to DeepSeek in DSH, with network access to `api.deepseek.com`.
- Node.js 22+ (the DSH desktop app bundles its own runtime).

dsh-deepseek-search-account README · Verifying and troubleshooting：`scripts/verify.mjs` runs the providers exactly as the harness does, using the real account token from `~/.dsh/.credentials.yaml` (the token never leaves the process):

dsh-deepseek-search-account README · Verifying and troubleshooting：```bash
NODE="/Applications/DeepSeek Harness.app/Contents/Resources/runtime/primary-runtime/dependencies/node/bin/node"
"$NODE" scripts/verify.mjs "query"                          # official Search API, ~0.4–0.6 s, snippets included
"$NODE" scripts/verify.mjs --fetch "https://example.com"    # official Fetch API, Markdown body
"$NODE" scripts/verify.mjs --fetch-fallback "<url>"         # official 403/404 triggers the local fallback

dsh-deepseek-search-account README · Verifying and troubleshooting：If search or fetch fails, the structured error names the cause: `WEB_PROVIDER_CREDENTIAL_MISSING` (not signed in and no API key), `WEB_PROVIDER_ERROR` (HTTP/network, with the endpoint that was used), `WEB_INVALID_URL` (fetch URL rejected before dispatch), `WEB_FETCH_TIMEOUT` (provider-side timeout), or `WEB_ABORTED` (cancelled). If the account sign-in is rejected, sign in to DeepSeek again — the endpoint does not need changing.

dsh-deepseek-search-account README · Uninstall：```bash
dsh plugin --profile desktop remove dsh-deepseek-search-account
```

This removes the package and its bundle layer; the profile's own search configuration is not touched. For the manual install, delete the two rows described above.
